intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene (600163) on chromosome 3p22.2. In 1 family, the disorder was associated with an SCN5A mutation coinherited with homozygosity for rare regulatory polymorphisms in the GJA5 gene (121013) on chromosome 1q21.2, consistent with digenic inheritance.

checks.claim: Atrial standstill-1 (ATRST1) is caused by mutation in the SCN5A gene.
checks.evidence_quote: In this study, familial AS was associated with the concurrence of a cardiac sodium channel mutation and rare polymorphisms in the atrial-specific Cx40 gene.
checks.explanation: The paper links an SCN5A mutation to familial atrial standstill, but it presents the disorder as associated with the SCN5A mutation together with Cx40 polymorphisms. It does not say the SCN5A mutation alone causes it.

checks.claim: The SCN5A gene is located on chromosome 3p22.2.
checks.evidence_quote: a novel mutation in the cardiac sodium channel gene SCN5A (D1275N)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to a gene the paper names, so it counts as a restatement.

checks.claim: In 1 family, atrial standstill was associated with an SCN5A mutation coinherited with homozygosity for rare regulatory polymorphisms in the GJA5 gene, consistent with digenic inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: The three living AS patients exclusively coinherited both the rare Cx40 genotype and the SCN5A-D1275N mutation.
checks.explanation: The paper reports homozygosity for regulatory polymorphisms in Cx40 (GJA5) coinherited with the SCN5A mutation and proposes a combined effect, which fits digenic inheritance.

checks.claim: The GJA5 gene is located on chromosome 1q21.2.
checks.evidence_quote: two closely linked polymorphisms were detected within regulatory regions of the gene for the atrial-specific gap junction protein connexin40 (Cx40)
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the Cx40 (GJA5) gene the paper names.

paragraphs.text: In a large family with atrial standstill, Groenewegen et al. (2003) used candidate gene screening to identify a novel mutation in the SCN5A gene, asp1275-to-asn (D1275N). The mutation was present in all 3 living affected relatives and in 5 unaffected relatives, and the deceased affected relative was an obligate carrier. Compared with wildtype channels, D1275N channels showed a small depolarizing shift in activation. Groenewegen et al. (2003) also found 2 closely linked polymorphisms in regulatory regions of the atrial-specific gap junction gene connexin-40 (GJA5), at nucleotides -44 (G-A) and +71 (A-G). Eight relatives were homozygous for both polymorphisms, and 3 of them were affected. This genotype was found in only about 7% of control subjects. In reporter gene analysis, the rare GJA5 genotype gave lower reporter expression than the more common genotype. The 3 living patients were the only relatives to have inherited both the rare GJA5 genotype and the SCN5A D1275N mutation. The authors proposed that each genetic change has a relatively benign functional effect, but that their combined effect eventually progresses to total atrial standstill.

paragraphs.text: In an 11-year-old boy with congenital atrial standstill, Makita et al. (2005) identified a novel SCN5A mutation, leu212-to-pro (L212P). His father, who was in normal sinus rhythm, also carried the mutation. The recombinant L212P channel was studied by whole-cell patch clamp in a heterologous expression system. It showed a large hyperpolarizing shift in the voltage dependence of activation (wildtype, -48.1 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -63.5 +/- 1.5 mV; P less than 0.001) and of inactivation (wildtype, -86.6 +/- 0.9 mV; L212P, -95.6 +/- 0.8 mV; P less than 0.001), as well as delayed recovery from inactivation. The proband, but not his father, also carried GJA5 polymorphisms inherited from his asymptomatic mother. Makita et al. (2005) concluded that SCN5A defects most likely underlie atrial standstill and that coinheritance of GJA5 polymorphisms may modify the clinical manifestation.
